surveillance_brief_p1: This operational dashboard provides real-time geographic and clinical surveillance on the 2026 Bundibugyo ebolavirus (BDBV) outbreak centered in northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), with active cross-border surveillance across the Albertine Rift corridor and western Uganda.
surveillance_brief_p2: Telemetry integrates verified epidemiological reports from the World Health Organization (WHO), Africa CDC, and the Humanitarian Data Exchange (UN OCHA).

symptoms_card_subtitle: Why early Ebola can resemble malaria, typhoid and other regional diseases
symptoms_intro: Ebola often begins with common, nonspecific symptoms. Bleeding is not always present, especially early in the illness.
symptoms_lookalike_title: Diseases considered in the affected region
symptoms_lookalike_malaria_overlap: Fever, headache, body aches, weakness and fatigue can look the same early on.
symptoms_lookalike_typhoid_overlap: Fever, headache, weakness and abdominal or digestive symptoms can overlap.
symptoms_lookalike_meningitis_overlap: Fever, severe headache, weakness and confusion can resemble Ebola symptoms.
symptoms_lookalike_shigellosis_overlap: Fever, abdominal pain and diarrhoea can resemble Ebola's gastrointestinal phase.
symptoms_lookalike_marburg_overlap: Another viral haemorrhagic fever that can cause a similar febrile and gastrointestinal illness.
symptoms_safety_body: Exposure history and laboratory testing are essential. If compatible symptoms follow a possible exposure, avoid direct contact with bodily fluids and contact local health authorities or a healthcare facility immediately. Call ahead if possible and follow their instructions. Do not wait for bleeding.
